description: Context.create unified-signature contract across all SDKs. Validates the v0.22.0 normative input list (identity, trace_parent, cancel_token, data, services, global_deadline), the removal of executor and caller_id as inputs, the Executor binding rules (local create, cross-process deserialize, hot-reload restore), and child() propagation. See docs/features/core-executor.md §Contract: Context.create + §Contract: Executor binding to Context, and Issue #66.

test_cases.description: Context.create() with no arguments yields a fresh top-level Context — null executor, null identity, null cancel_token, empty data, empty call_chain, null caller_id, 32-char hex trace_id.
Most common adapter pattern: only identity supplied. trace_id auto-generated, all other caller-inputs null.
cancel_token is a first-class parameter (v0.22.0+). Verifies the token is carried on the returned Context without post-hoc assignment.
global_deadline is an accepted caller input. Local-only — does not affect serialize round-trip (see context_create_distributed).

executor MUST NOT be a public Context.create() parameter. SDKs MAY enforce by signature (no such parameter exists) or by runtime check. Either is conforming as long as 'pass executor at construction' is not possible through the public API.
caller_id MUST NOT be a public Context.create() parameter. Top-level Contexts always have caller_id = null; the field is managed exclusively by Context.child().

Local construction → first Executor.call() succeeds (i.e. binding does not raise). The exact post-call observability of ctx.executor varies by SDK: some SDKs clone the Context into the pipeline (Rust) or treat it as immutable per call (TypeScript's copy-on-write), so the caller-held reference may still report `executor = null` after the call returns. Conforming behavior is that the binding succeeded and the call ran — not that the original reference observed the mutation. SDKs MAY additionally expose an SDK-private hook to verify pre-step-1 binding for internal testing.

notes.non_normative: Pre-step-1 binding and post-call executor visibility on the caller's reference are implementation-detail concerns. The normative contract is that the call runs without ContextBindingError when ctx.executor is null at entry.

test_cases.description: Reusing the same Context across multiple top-level Executor.call() invocations on the same Executor instance is a noop on subsequent calls — MUST NOT raise.

ctx.executor is bound to Executor A; Executor B receives the same Context and MUST raise ContextBindingError. Was `expected_one_of` with a silent-accept alternative: all three SDKs take the raise branch (apcore-python context.py:152, apcore-typescript context.ts:187, apcore-rust context.rs:765), so the alternative permitted a deviation nobody took while making the case unassertable — every driver hardcoded 'raise' and read the alternation only in a comment.
Context.child() MUST propagate the bound executor to the child Context.
Context.child() MUST propagate the cancel_token to the child Context. Same reference (or equivalent linked instance) — modules deep in the call chain MUST observe cancellation.

Cross-process scenario: deserialize a serialized Context (executor / cancel_token / services / global_deadline all stripped per §5.7), then call() on the receiving node. The local Executor MUST bind itself per the same rule as local Context.create().

Negative invariant: cancel_token MUST NOT serialize (per PROTOCOL_SPEC §5.7). A deserialized Context arriving on a remote node has cancel_token = null. The normative requirement that the receiving Executor synthesizes a fresh local CancelToken at pipeline entry is an SDK-internal implementation detail — not directly observable through the public Context API, so this fixture asserts only the externally visible invariant (`cancel_token` field is null after deserialize). SDKs SHOULD additionally verify the synthesis behavior through SDK-private tests.

notes.implementation_detail: Pipeline-entry CancelToken synthesis is normative (MUST) but not asserted here because the synthesized token is internal to pipeline Step 2 and not exposed on the post-call caller-held Context reference.

test_cases.description: Negative invariant: global_deadline MUST NOT serialize. A deserialized Context arriving on a remote node has global_deadline = null. The receiving Executor recomputes global_deadline from local executor.global_timeout config (implementation detail tested SDK-internally). This fixture asserts only the serialization-level invariant.

notes.implementation_detail: Local recomputation from executor.global_timeout config is normative (MUST) but tested via the existing dual-timeout fixtures rather than re-asserted here. Callers needing a wall-clock deadline across process boundaries SHOULD store the absolute timestamp in context.data under an extension key.

test_cases.description: TraceParent type MUST carry tracestate as a field (no separate Context.create() parameter). Verifies cross-SDK shape: Python/TS/Rust all embed tracestate in TraceParent.

driver_contract.assert_the_wire_code: `error_code` is the contract. `ContextBindingError` is a class name apcore-python and apcore-typescript share and apcore-rust does not have — it has ErrorCode::ContextBindingError — so a class-name assertion is green on two SDKs and unwritable on the third.
driver_contract.one_behaviour_not_two: This case previously carried `expected_one_of: [raise, silent_accept]`. A driver cannot assert an alternation without deciding which branch its SDK takes, so all three hardcoded the branch and never read the fixture — mutating the whole block left every suite green. If an SDK ever needs the silent-accept behaviour again, that is a spec change, not a fixture alternation.
